problem_markdown: For every positive integer $d\notin\{2,5,13\}$, prove some distinct $a,b\in\{2,5,13,d\}$ make $ab-1$ nonsquare.
solutions_markdown: Suppose $2d-1,5d-1,13d-1$ were all squares. Squares modulo sixteen lie in $\{0,1,4,9\}$. The first condition forces $d\equiv1,5,9,13\pmod{16}$. For $d\equiv1$ or 13, $13d-1$ has residue 12 or 8, impossible for a square. For $d\equiv5$ or 9, $5d-1$ has residue 8 or 12, also impossible. Hence at least one of the three products involving $d$ is nonsquare. Its two factors are distinct by the hypothesis on $d$.
